niche_preference_profile: Prefers interfaces with strong hierarchy, clear structure, and visibly purposeful content. They consistently like layouts that feel polished, segmented, and actionable, with prominent controls, defined cards or grouped sections, and enough populated information to avoid looking empty. They often respond well to premium, editorial styling: bold titles, atmospheric imagery, refined spacing, and cohesive visual systems. Their color preference is context-dependent: in settings and utility screens they often favor light, airy, soft-toned presentations, while in denser management or privacy flows they sometimes prefer darker, higher-contrast, more dramatic treatments when those improve hierarchy, depth, and personality.

criteria.description: Prefers screens with clear top-down hierarchy, strong focal points, bold titles, and obvious differentiation between primary and secondary information.
Prefers content that is cleanly organized into coherent sections, cards, or grouped modules with consistent separation rather than fragmented or weakly structured layouts.
Prefers interfaces where primary actions and per-item controls are immediately visible, prominent, and purpose-built rather than hidden or passive.
Prefers refined, internally consistent, finished-looking interfaces with cohesive component styling and fewer awkward or unresolved details.
Prefers larger, bolder, more editorial headline treatment and stronger typographic framing over smaller, flatter, app-default titles.
Prefers designs that include human or expressive elements such as real photos, avatars, colorful identity markers, or lifestyle-oriented imagery that add warmth and character.
Prefers screens that feel populated and concrete, with enough visible content, metadata, and specificity to communicate function clearly rather than appearing empty or vague.
